editorial:
Ever wonder why some people just don't seem to like you? That is exactly where you start with this funny and awkward story. You follow a guy played by Albert Brooks who is tired of being disliked, so he decides to go to a professional research institute. He wants to use science to figure out his personality flaws and learn how to be more likable. The vibe is very dry and sarcastic, making you feel like you are watching a social experiment gone wrong. It feels like a conversation with a friend who is trying way too hard to fit in, which makes it both cringe-worthy and hilarious.

What really works here is how Brooks plays the character as someone who thinks he is the smartest person in the room, even while he is paying people to tell him he is annoying. The pacing is quick, and the dialogue feels very natural. If you enjoy comedy that pokes fun at human nature, you will love this. Since it is an older piece, you can find it in various archives or as part of SNL collections.
endingExplained: By the end, you see that the main character has not actually changed at all. Even after all the research and feedback, he remains just as arrogant and stubborn as he was at the start. He tries to apply the lessons he learned, but he does it in a way that is still annoying to everyone around him. The joke is that he thinks he is fixing himself, but he is actually just becoming a more polished version of the same guy.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dry humor and character studies.
